_items_source.document: AQA GCSE German (8662) specification, first teaching September 2024: themes 3.1, grammar 3.2, vocabulary 3.3
_items_source.version: Specification for first teaching from September 2024, linked from aqa.org.uk/8662, itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: AQA numbers the three themes and their three topics each (3.1.1-3.1.3 per theme) but presents the content under each topic, and the whole of 3.2 Grammar, as unnumbered bullet lists. This course codes the eighteen topic-content items by theme.topic and a letter in AQA's own bullet order (e.g. T1.1a, T1.1b for Theme 1 Topic 1), and codes the sixteen grammar points G1-G16 in a logical teaching order built from the specification's own Foundation/Higher split (Foundation content first, then the Higher-tier additions folded into the same numbered point where they extend the same structure), plus five items (LIS.1, SPK.1, SPK.2, RDG.1, WRT.1) for the exam-skill content of each of the four papers, which AQA sets out in its scheme of assessment rather than as numbered subject content.

_syllabus_items.title: Nouns: gender, compound-noun formation, plural formation, nominalised infinitives
Definite/indefinite articles and the nominative, accusative and dative cases; negation with kein
Other determiners (dieser/jeder/welcher, possessive adjectives, quantifiers) across the three cases
Personal pronouns (subject, accusative, dative) and the interrogative pronoun wer/wen/wem
Reflexive pronouns and reflexive verbs; relative pronouns in subject relative clauses
Present tense (weak and strong verbs, haben/sein/werden/wissen) and question formation
Perfect tense, including past-participle formation patterns and haben/sein as auxiliary
Future tense (werden + infinitive) and modal verbs, including möchte
Word order: verb-second in main clauses, verb-final in subordinate clauses, separable verbs, negation with nicht/kein/nie
Adjective endings after definite/indefinite articles and with no article, in the nominative, accusative and dative
Comparative and superlative adjectives/adverbs, and adverb position
Accusative, dative and two-way prepositions, their contractions, and da-/wo- compounds
Higher tier: the genitive case, dative plural nouns, plural object pronouns, and word order in two-verb subordinate clauses
Higher tier: the imperfect/simple past for narrative, and the imperative
Higher tier: um/ohne/statt...zu infinitive constructions, the man-passive-avoidance structure, and the conditional (würde/hätte/wäre)
Higher tier: derivational morphology for reading (un-, -heit/-keit, -los, -chen/-lein, -ung, agent nouns in -er, Lieblings-/Haupt-)
Listening strategies and dictation
Speaking: role-play and reading aloud
Speaking: photo card discussion and unprepared conversation
Reading strategies and translation into English
Writing tasks, translation into German and extended writing
